requirements.statement: The choice between the related Game Problems must depend on the interaction circumstances. A primary or secondary designation made for one execution is not a permanent hierarchy between them.
words: Create Space and Exploit Space should not have a permanent hierarchical relationship simply because one is designated primary in this particular execution.
When an organized defense is meaningfully restricting available space, creating additional opportunities may be the dominant problem.
When useful space is already available, exploiting it may be the immediate problem. Players shouldn't be encouraged to create space unnecessarily.
The selected Game Problem should ultimately depend on the interaction circumstances, not simply the wording of the Learning Goal.

laws.reason: The ordinary kickoff at the start and after a point (Christian's provisional option); the centre mark and halfway line it needs are marked (illustrative).
A stoppage the coach makes restarts with a dropped ball, as in the Laws; nothing departs from it.
No offside: Christian's provisional ruling, explicitly communicated.
There is no goalkeeper, so no goalkeeper handling; no player may handle the ball.
No goal stands at either end, so there is no penalty kick.

Free kicks as in the Laws; nothing departs from them. Review point (OURS): a free kick next to a target zone keeps the opponents 9.15 m from the ball, which can leave the zone empty for an immediate point; no rule is invented (listed in Part 3 as a known risk).

Throw-ins as in the Laws; nothing departs from them. Review point (OURS): a throw-in beside a target zone, to a teammate standing in it, could give an immediate point, although the Laws allow no goal straight from a throw-in; no rule is invented (listed in Part 3 as a known risk).

The goal kick restarts a ball over the end line but assumes a goal and its goal area; there is no goal here, so an adaptation is owed. The ILLUSTRATIVE end-line value stands in (the team defending the target zone at that end restarts from that end line), pending Christian's confirmation. Review point (OURS): the Laws keep opponents outside the penalty area until a goal kick is in play; nothing here does, and that end line is the back edge of the target zone the opponents attack, so an opponent standing in that zone who intercepts the restart and controls the ball there scores at once; no rule is invented (listed in Part 3 as a known risk).

The corner kick restarts a ball over the end line but assumes a goal with a corner area beside it; there is no goal here, so an adaptation is owed. A corner kick would also be taken inside a target zone, where a pass to a teammate could give an immediate point (review point, OURS). The same ILLUSTRATIVE end-line value stands in, pending Christian's confirmation.

reviewPoints.statement: Attackers may wait inside the target zone for a pass: a risk Christian has seen in similar games (said of the build-out activity, 15 October). Applying it here is ours (OURS: CAUSAL HYPOTHESIS). No mechanism is imposed, as Christian's words ask; it bears on meaningful opposition and on multiple functional solutions, and is visible only in play.

A restart taken beside or inside a target zone could give an immediate point: a throw-in to a teammate standing in the zone; a free kick next to it, which keeps the opponents 9.15 m from the ball; a corner kick, were one taken. The Laws apply unchanged and no rule is invented; the end-line value has the team defending a target zone restart from its own end line, on the back edge of the zone its opponents attack; with no opponent distance added, an opponent standing in that zone who intercepts the restart and controls the ball there scores at once. Visible only in play.

openDecisions.question: May the illustrative end-line restart stand in this offline example? Is that acceptable, or would you prefer a coach-served ball there ("a coach quickly serving a new ball can be an effective way to maintain game flow, energy, and the frequency of meaningful opportunities"), not treated as a live turnover?
